featured_reviews.name: Khushrav A
featured_reviews.review_text:
Very sad to state that We were disappointed this last weekend with Family and Friends when we called food from I'm Wholesome.
1. A Bulk order was placed at 6:27pm on Swiggy for delivery
2. At 730pm when we check with Swiggy about the order, the delivery agent informed that due to size of the order, he cannot carry the full order.
3. We reach out to Customer care who connect us with delivery agent and wholesome team. We discussed the transport issues and at 830pm Swiggy agreed to send the order in another 22mins while the person from the Wholesome Team confirmed that half order is already dispatched with first order while Swiggy confirmed that second rider is being arranged asap.

****Best Part is that Wholesome team confirmed they had not prepared the order till 8:15pm since they had lots of orders and mine was a termed as Bulk order***

4. After all this confirmations from Swiggy and Wholesome team the App notifies the whole order is cancelled and refund is issued.

Such was the empathy towards the customer and disrespectful way of doing business.

It also contributed to an unfortunate situation which caused my guest to wait another order and be fed with more than 2 hrs of delay.

I know this comment may not go well with reviewers and wholesome team, but somewhere Wholesome team is responsible since the false communication being passed on to their customer plus their food Partner Swiggy cannot help them with a classification of "Bulk Order"
No compensation , No apology, Just a refund.

featured_reviews.review_text:
This place is more than just a fish market to me — it carries years of memories. Since childhood, this has always been my go-to place for the freshest fish, and every visit feels like returning to a part of old Bombay.

What made this place special was not only the quality of the catch but also the culture around it. Back in the day, people from all over — from Juhu to Bandra — would visit. It was known not just among locals but had stories connected to well-known personalities, film stars, government offices, and generations of loyal customers. There was a warmth here that made it feel more like a community than a market.

But time changes everything. Fishing has reduced, many traditional fisherfolk families have moved away from the profession, and the younger generation has chosen education and new career paths to build different futures. It’s understandable and part of progress, though it brings a sense of nostalgia for those who remember the old days.

Even today, this place remains special — not because it stayed the same, but because it carries the history, hard work, and memories of a community that helped shape this part of the city.

If you want fresh fish with a story behind it, this place is still worth visiting.

featured_reviews.name: Biswajit
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visit Khar Danda Fish Market regularly and it’s one of the best places in Mumbai to buy fresh fish. The fish quality is very good as it comes directly from fishermen, especially if you go early morning.
Prices are much cheaper compared to supermarkets, but bargaining is very important here. If you have good negotiation skills, you can get really great deals.
There is a wide variety of fish available like pomfret, surmai, prawns, and more. Sellers also help with cleaning and cutting.
Only downside is hygiene and crowd, but that’s normal for a local fish market.
Overall, highly recommended for fresh and budget-friendly fish 👍

featured_reviews.name: Tiven Gonsalves (Tiven2240)
featured_reviews.review_text: Trombay fish market is one of the oldest market in Mumbai. It has a variety of fish available for Sale in it's market. The variety of prawns and other fishes too were found here. Trombay fish market has a connectivity of Bus which has the direct accessibility to this place. The birhanmumbai municipal corporation and the birhanmumbai electrical supply and transport along with the forest department and Indian Navy have a strong hold over this place. The place is well maintained by local villagers who have made a concrete platform for them to sell fish in very large quantity. The market starts from 7.30-8.00 am in the morning and gets wind up at around 10 in the morning. After that the local fishing community have their trade of fishing at the market which has been developed for them on the coast of the Village. The villagers are very cooperative and have a fragile nature. They are very good to interact with others and provide personalised experience to the other people's who visit this place.
